content.prompt: The diagram shows a quarter circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ divided into five strips of equal width. Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate its area. Hence estimate $\pi$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
The circle has equation $x^2+y^2=25$, so the heights are $y=\sqrt{25-x^2}$. At $x=0,1,2,3,4,5$ these are $5,\sqrt{24},\sqrt{21},4,3,0$, and $h=1$.
$$\begin{align*}A&\approx\frac{1}{2}\bigl[5+0+2(\sqrt{24}+\sqrt{21}+4+3)\bigr]\\&\approx18.98\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
The area of the quarter circle is $\dfrac{\pi\times5^2}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{25\pi}{4}&\approx18.98\\\pi&\approx\frac{4\times18.98}{25}\\&\approx3.04\end{align*}$$
